questions.q: What is the process of 'ingestion' defined as?
a: Taking food into the body through the mouth
Breaking down large food molecules
Absorbing nutrients into the blood
Passing out unabsorbed waste

questions.q: What is mechanical digestion?
a: The chemical breakdown of food by enzymes
The breakdown of large food pieces into smaller pieces without chemical change to the molecules, increasing surface area
The absorption of water in the colon
The active transport of glucose

questions.q: What occurs during chemical digestion?
a: Food is chewed by teeth into smaller chunks
Stomach muscles churn food mechanically
Large, insoluble food molecules are broken down into small, soluble molecules by digestive enzymes
Food is moved along the gut by peristalsis

questions.q: What is the definition of 'absorption' in the digestive system?
a: The swallowing of food boluses
The removal of feces from the anus
The building of proteins from amino acids
The movement of small, soluble food molecules and ions through the wall of the intestine into the blood or lymph

questions.q: What is 'assimilation'?
a: The uptake and incorporation of absorbed food molecules into body tissues to become part of the cells
The breakdown of fats by bile
The physical chewing of food in the mouth
The storage of feces in the rectum

questions.q: What is 'egestion'?
a: The excretion of urea through the kidneys
The passing out of food that has not been digested or absorbed, as feces, through the anus
The secretion of saliva into the mouth
The release of sweat from skin pores

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the organs of the human alimentary canal in the correct order of food passage?
a: Mouth -> Stomach -> Esophagus -> Small intestine -> Large intestine -> Anus
Mouth -> Small intestine -> Stomach -> Esophagus -> Rectum
Mouth -> Esophagus -> Stomach -> Small intestine -> Large intestine -> Rectum -> Anus
Stomach -> Mouth -> Esophagus -> Colon -> Anus

questions.q: What is the function of peristalsis along the alimentary canal?
a: To secrete hydrochloric acid
To digest starch into maltose
To absorb water into the bloodstream
To push food along the gut through alternating waves of contraction and relaxation of circular and longitudinal muscles

questions.q: Where does mechanical digestion primarily begin in the human digestive tract?
a: In the mouth, via the action of teeth chewing food
In the esophagus
In the stomach lining
In the duodenum

questions.q: What enzyme is present in human saliva, and what substrate does it break down?
a: Pepsin; breaks down proteins
Amylase; breaks down starch into maltose
Lipase; breaks down lipids
Trypsin; breaks down polypeptides

questions.q: What is the role of hydrochloric acid found in gastric juice within the stomach?
a: To digest dietary fiber completely
To absorb water molecules
To kill harmful bacteria ingested with food and provide the optimum acidic pH (around pH 2) for the protease enzyme pepsin
To neutralize bile from the liver

questions.q: Which organ produces bile, and where is bile stored before being released into the small intestine?
a: Produced in the pancreas; stored in the stomach
Produced in the spleen; stored in the appendix
Produced in the kidneys; stored in the bladder
Produced in the liver; stored in the gall bladder

questions.q: What are the two primary functions of bile in the digestive process?
a: Emulsifying fats to increase surface area for lipase action, and neutralizing stomach acid to provide an alkaline pH in the duodenum
Digesting starch into glucose
Absorbing amino acids into blood capillaries
Killing stomach bacteria with strong acid

questions.q: What enzyme secreted by the pancreas breaks down proteins into smaller peptides in the small intestine?
a: Amylase
Trypsin
Maltase
Lipase

questions.q: How is the structure of the small intestine (specifically the ileum) specially adapted for efficient absorption of digested food molecules?
a: It has thick muscular walls that prevent diffusion
It is coated in a thick waterproof wax
It possesses millions of villi and microvilli, providing a huge surface area, a rich capillary network, and a short diffusion distance
It secretes hydrochloric acid to dissolve nutrients

questions.q: What is the primary function of the large intestine (colon and rectum)?
a: Producing bile and digestive enzymes
Absorbing digested glucose
Filtering urea from blood
Absorbing remaining water from undigested food residue and storing feces

questions.q: What is the role of lacteals found inside the villi of the small intestine?
a: Absorbing and transporting fatty acids and glycerol into the lymphatic system
Absorbing water and mineral ions
Secreting digestive enzymes
Producing red blood cells

questions.q: Which of the following enzymes completes the breakdown of maltose into glucose in the small intestine?
a: Pepsin
Maltase
Amylase
Lipase

questions.q: Why is the stomach lining protected from being digested by its own acidic pepsin enzymes?
a: Because the stomach contains no protein
Because stomach cells do not respire
Because specialized goblet cells secrete a thick layer of mucus lining the stomach wall
Because hydrochloric acid neutralizes the stomach walls

questions.q: What is the name of the muscular ring that controls the passage of food from the stomach into the duodenum?
a: Ileocecal valve
Anal sphincter
Cardiac sphincter
Pyloric sphincter

questions.q: Which accessory organ of the digestive system produces insulin, glucagon, and a comprehensive fluid containing amylase, trypsin, and lipase?
a: Pancreas
Liver
Gall bladder
Salivary gland

questions.q: How do amino acids and glucose absorbed from the small intestine travel directly to the liver?
a: Via the lymphatic vessel (lacteal)
Via the hepatic portal vein
Via the renal artery
Via the pulmonary vein

questions.q: What happens to excess amino acids absorbed into the liver that cannot be stored or used for protein synthesis?
a: They are converted into starch
They are passed out in feces
They undergo deamination, where the nitrogen-containing amino group is removed and converted into urea
They are exhaled as nitrogen gas

questions.q: Which of the following correctly pairs a digestive enzyme with its site of production and action?
a: Pepsin — produced in pancreas, acts in mouth
Amylase — produced in stomach, acts in liver
Lipase — produced in large intestine, acts in colon
Amylase — produced in salivary glands and pancreas, acts in mouth and small intestine

questions.q: What is the role of the hepatic portal vein?
a: Transporting nutrient-rich blood directly from the capillary beds of the intestines to the liver for processing and regulation
Carrying oxygenated blood from the heart to the gut
Draining deoxygenated blood from kidneys
Transporting fats through the lymphatic system

questions.q: What causes gallstones to form in some individuals?
a: Excess stomach acid corrosion
Hardened deposits of digestive fluid (cholesterol or bile pigments) forming in the gall bladder
Infection by bacteriophage viruses
Lack of dietary fiber causing constipation

questions.q: What is the main function of the canine and incisor teeth in humans?
a: Grinding and crushing food
Producing saliva
Biting, cutting, and tearing pieces of food during ingestion
Swallowing food boluses

questions.q: Which of the following describes the physical structure of a human tooth crown?
a: Covered in soft cementum and pulp
Composed entirely of living blood vessels
Rooted directly into the jawbone without enamel
Covered in hard enamel, protecting the underlying dentine and central pulp cavity containing nerves and blood vessels

questions.q: What causes tooth decay (dental caries)?
a: Bacteria in dental plaque feeding on sugary food residues, producing acid that dissolves tooth enamel and dentine
A deficiency of Vitamin C in the diet
Mechanical abrasion from chewing tough meat
Excess saliva production

questions.q: How does the structure of a villus capillary network maintain a steep concentration gradient for absorption?
a: Blood flows slowly, allowing nutrients to accumulate
Constant blood flow through capillaries carries absorbed glucose and amino acids away, maintaining a low concentration in the blood relative to the gut lumen
Capillaries actively push nutrients back into the gut
Capillaries are impermeable to water

questions.q: What role do goblet cells play in the lining of the alimentary canal?
a: Absorbing digested fats
Secreting hydrochloric acid
Secreting mucus to lubricate the food passage and protect gut walls
Producing digestive enzymes

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of assimilation in human nutrition?
a: Chewing food in the mouth
Swallowing a bolus of food down the esophagus
Egesting feces through the anus
Absorbed glucose being used in cells for respiration or converted into glycogen for storage in liver cells

questions.q: What is the main purpose of emulsification of fats by bile salts?
a: To break large fat globules into tiny oil droplets, massively increasing the surface area for lipase enzymes to act upon
To convert fats into proteins
To dissolve fats into water permanently
To kill bacteria in lipid foods

questions.q: Which condition is characterized by watery feces caused by infection or toxins that reduce water absorption in the large intestine?
a: Constipation
Diarrhea
Appendicitis
Gastric ulcer

questions.q: What is the function of the epiglottis during swallowing?
a: To produce saliva in the throat
To open the airway for breathing
To fold down and cover the trachea (windpipe), preventing food and liquid from entering the lungs
To secrete protease enzymes

questions.q: Which of the following describes the correct pH environment for enzymes in the stomach versus the small intestine?
a: Stomach: alkaline (pH 8); Small intestine: acidic (pH 2)
Stomach: neutral (pH 7); Small intestine: neutral (pH 7)
Stomach: acidic (pH 2); Small intestine: acidic (pH 3)
Stomach: acidic (pH 2); Small intestine: alkaline (pH 8)

questions.q: What happens to food inside the mouth during chewing before it is swallowed?
a: It is mechanically broken down by teeth, mixed with saliva containing mucus and amylase, and formed into a lubricated bolus
It is completely digested into individual amino acids
It is sterilized by hydrochloric acid
It is absorbed directly into cheek capillaries

questions.q: Which part of the digestive system secretes succus entericus (intestinal juice containing maltase, peptidase, etc.)?
a: The stomach lining
The walls of the small intestine
The pancreas
The liver

questions.q: What is the primary cause of stomach ulcers (peptic ulcers)?
a: Eating spicy food too quickly
Excess physical exercise after meals
Infection by the bacterium *Helicobacter pylori*, which breaks down the protective mucus lining
Lack of dietary fiber

questions.q: Which term describes the elimination of undigested waste material via the anus?
a: Excretion
Secretion
Assimilation
Egestion
